svg.text: 5 · Downstream workflows run concurrently and trade outputs — the cross-edges are the science
Four analysis programmes that can all start once diagram 3 delivers a GFF. Run in isolation each produces a list; the value is in what they hand each other.
in all four lanes at once —
turns 'which genes exist' into 'which genes vary'
produces intervals; only the last two steps produce genes
free from data already collected for the assembly
the triangle the guide had two corners of and no edges
SV + PAV matrix becomes the genotype input — this is how SV-GWAS actually happens
mQTL as an intermediate phenotype for colocalisation
is the BGC in an active compartment?
All four lanes can start the day the GFF lands, so a Gantt
chart shows them side by side with no dependencies.
But lane B is weak without lane A's SV matrix, lane D is
guesswork without lane B's validated locus, and lane C
is the only one that costs nothing extra to run.
Sequence them by what they owe each other, not by when

Every lane ends in something publishable on its own, which is exactly why cross-lane trades get skipped — each team ships its list and stops. The red edges are the parts that are nobody's deliverable and where nearly all the causal claims actually come from.
